data: Fleet launch-site entry added during the LL2 cross-correlation analysis (#306 follow-up). Originally Titan III / Titan IV; rebuilt for Atlas V (2002-) and the pad Vulcan Centaur has flown from since January 2024. ~95 historic launches in our manifest mapped here.
SLC-41 historic and current operations (Space Force)
Atlas V's main pad — flew every Atlas V mission including Mars Perseverance + Lucy + Starliner CFT

United Launch Alliance's primary Atlas V pad at Cape Canaveral, originally built for Titan III in the 1960s, entirely demolished in 1999 and rebuilt as the Atlas V pad; first Atlas V flight 2002-08-21. Every Atlas V flight has launched from here — Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter, Curiosity, Perseverance, Lucy, Juno, the Boeing Starliner Crew Flight Test, and dozens of NSSL national-security missions. Also hosts Vulcan Centaur, which began flying from SLC-41 in January 2024.

USSF reusable robotic spaceplane — multi-year classified orbital missions, the only US spaceplane operational after the Shuttle's retirement
Highest-cadence Falcon 9 pad on the planet — workhorse for ISS resupply + Starlink + national-security
USAF Atlas-Centaur pad — Mariner 10, Pioneer 11 (1973), Pioneer Venus (1978); now Blue Origin New Glenn (leased 2015, flew 2025)
France's first satellite, Astérix, launched on a Diamant A in 1965
